text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Prime Minister Abdul Salam al-Majali pledges support of Jordan to Palestinians during a meeting with a Palestinian official; says the Palestinian issue on top of the kingdom's concerns and Amman will do utmost to help Palestinians to attain their national aspirations.
- Crown Prince Hassan stresses in a speech to a seminar on diplomacy "the importance of attaining security in its broad concept."
- Snow covers mountain caps and rains spread across the kingdom in unusual weather conditions, but gradually warm weather as temperature rise is expected later on Friday.

- Crown Prince Hassan receives in royal court Saed Kamal, the Arab League's assistant general secretary; they discuss latest developments in the Middle East peace process and means of advancing Arab-Israeli peace.

- Opposition parties reach initial agreement to participate in the coming parliamentary elections due in November in one united front; sources say hardliners in the powerful Islamic Action Front (IAF) are against the move while moderates are in favour of closing ranks with smaller leftist parties.
- Pharmacists to elect on Friday both a new head of their union and a new board to represent them; 24 candidates competing for 10 board seats and three for the post of union head.

- Nursing students at Jordan's University Medical College plan to suspend studies on Saturday in protest over unreadiness of the university administration to heed demands relating to their work conditions.
